subject: Mid-contract uplift: alternative tiering & procurement timing
messages:

Cc: procurement@lyrahealth.com

Subject: Exploring a mid-year top-up and alternate pricing tiers

Hi Rafael,

We kicked off a planning sync this morning and expect a sustained usage increase across our triage and patient-summary flows. We don't want to wait until renewal to lock this in — we need ~60% additional capacity for the next 6 months while we finish a migration.

Could Redwood support a mid-contract uplift without forcing a full annual re-commit? Ideally we'd: 1) keep a short-term uplift for 6 months, 2) get a credits/discount that phases into our renewal, and 3) align invoices to our procurement quarter (PO window is mid-Oct).

I've attached a draft SOW with expected headroom and a rough PO timeline (Lyra_SOW_draft_v1.pdf). Quick questions: what discounting levers do you typically use for a mid-contract top-up? Any co-term pitfalls we should plan for?

Appreciate any options you can share — happy to jump on a 20-min call this week.

Thanks,
Alex Morales
Head of Integrations, LyraHealth
Alex.Morales@lyrahealth.com

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. I read through the numbers; there are a couple practical ways we can address this without a full annualization today. High level options below (happy to expand during a quick call):

Option A — Temporary top-up (fast):
- 6-month uplift at current hosted rates with a 7% credit applied to overage tokens for that window.
- No change to your renewal date (keeps current co-term).
- Good if you want minimal procurement friction and predictable month-to-month billing.

Option B — Bridge + partial annualize (recommended if you expect to keep higher usage):
- Apply a 30% commitment of the uplift as a 12-month annualized add-on, with the remaining 70% treated as a 6-month trial uplift.
- Earn a 10% blended credit applied immediately and an additional 5% at renewal if annualization sticks.
- Allows procurement to approve a smaller longer-term commitment now and reduces sticker shock at renewal.

Notes / Pitfalls:
- Co-terming mid-contract is doable, but be explicit about which capacity is "trial" vs "committed" — otherwise finance/proration can be messy.
- Procurement PO windows are fine; we'll align invoice cadence but need a signed statement of work or amendment before the uplift goes live.

I cc'ed Marissa from Commercial to weigh in on trade-offs and approvals. If you want, I can draft the amendment language for your legal/procurement team and include an invoice timing appendix for mid-Oct PO.

Would Thursday 10–10:30 PT work for a quick sync?

Best,
Rafael Mendes

Alex / Rafael — quick commercial overlay from my side.

Thanks for the SOW — we can be flexible here. Two practical plays we typically use for customers in this situation:

1) Short-term bridge credit (no renewal move): 8–10% credit on uplifted usage for the 6-month period. This keeps the renewal unchanged and is easiest for procurement.

2) Partial annualization with ramp incentives: convert up to 40% of the uplift into an annual add-on now (lower blended rate), with an additional onboarding credit if Lyra hits 80% of uplifted capacity for 90 consecutive days. That onboarding credit is a one-time bill credit (applied to first invoice after renewal).

For Lyra specifically, given your PO cadence, I'd suggest Option 2 but structured to minimize procurement approvals: we draft an amendment that highlights the 40% annualized commitment and a 6-month trial for the rest. If procurement needs a shorter approval cycle, we can provide a two-invoice approach so Oct PO covers the trial months and the annualized piece starts once DocuSign is returned.

I'll prepare a short amendment template (shows numbers + invoice timing) and a DocuSign packet.

Ben — can you confirm we can offer the 10% trial credit for 6 months and the additional onboarding credit tied to usage? Also confirm finance prefers a single or split invoice for the Oct PO.

- Marissa

All — quick finance note. We can do the 10% trial credit for six months (applied as a line-item credit). For the partial annualization (40%): finance prefers a single annualized amendment if procurement can sign before the end of Oct; if procurement needs a split approval we can issue two invoices (trial months covered by Oct PO, annualized commitment invoiced separately once fully executed).

The blended rate when annualizing 40% will be ~12% below current list for that portion (this is due to the committed capacity discount and expected token profile). I attached a preview for internal numbers (invoice_preview.xlsx).
